raw_segments.text: You, I replied, have in your mind a truly sublime conception of our knowledge of the
And I dare say that if a person were to throw his head back and study the fretted ceiling,
you would still think that his mind was the percipient, and not his eyes.
And you are very likely right, and I may be a simpleton.
But in my opinion, that knowledge only which is of being and of the unseen can make the
soul look upwards, and whether a man gapes at the heavens or blinks on the ground, seeking
to learn some particular of sense, I would deny that he can learn, for nothing of that
His soul is looking downwards, not upwards, whether his way to knowledge is by water or
by land, whether he floats, or only lies on his back.
